title: Multimodal Collaborative Agents for Next-Gen Commerce — Nidhi Kaushik Vyas, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: A Google DeepMind product talk on shopping agents that handle fuzzy user intent through a three-phase loop: discovery (build a working state of hard/soft constraints and pick the highest-information-gain next question), multimodal elicitation (ask with visual boards rather than text when preferences are subjective), and adaptive response formatting (tables/lists/visuals matched to the query). The transferable core is the evaluation discipline: per-phase auto-raters (fact retention, counterfactual sensitivity, over-asking, turn efficiency, format accuracy) that grow with the system.

takeaways.technique: Per-phase auto-raters that evolve with the system
takeaways.what_they_do: They attach a small set of auto-raters to each stage of the agent loop rather than one end-to-end score, and explicitly treat the rater set as something that grows as the system changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: developing these auto raters is a is is almost like an evolving system. It starts very simple, but as and when you start the the system starts evolving, you want the auto raters to kind of gradually grow

takeaways.what_they_do: They perturb parts of the input query and verify that the extracted constraints that should change do change and the irrelevant ones stay fixed, measuring sensitivity in both directions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we do this by flipping some parts of the queries and making sure that when the query changes, the underlying constraints pulled out by the agent the those also change and the ones that are not relevant stay the same

takeaways.what_they_do: Before asking the user anything, the agent enumerates unknown variables, scores candidate questions by how much they would change the outcome, and asks only the top one — explicitly penalizing over-asking.
takeaways.evidence_quote: figure out what is that one unknown variable that it should prioritize such that it has the maximal information gain at that point

takeaways.technique: Explicit working state with hard vs soft constraints and confidence
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent maintains a structured working state per session: session history, user context, hard constraints, soft constraints inferred from references, plus a confidence score and a list of variables needing real-time refresh.
takeaways.evidence_quote: some of the things that the agent develops as part of the working state is the session history. It has a user context. It also kind of extracts out the hard constraint

takeaways.technique: Format selection matched to query type
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent chooses the response format (bulleted summary, comparison table, visual board) based on what the user is trying to do, and they rate format-selection accuracy as a first-class metric.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the user was looking more towards comparing two different products, maybe the best response is to give out a trade-off table or a comparison table

takeaways.what_they_do: They drive the agent with a simulated user seeded with hidden constraints and measure how many turns it takes to uncover them, flagging repeated or low-utility questions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we would use a user simulator, feed it with some constraints, and then we'll see how how efficient the agent was in kind of eliciting some of these constraints
